claim: GPS-style means-ends (pick operator by named difference, push precondition subgoals) is a fixed loop that code can run while the model fills only the difference-naming and operator slots.
agent_test: Arm A: code-held loop with model filling slots vs arm B: free CoT, equal tokens, on Blocksworld-style and ARC items.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The quality of the difference-operator table decides GPS success; the table was hand-made, and no study measured tolerance to a wrong table. Indirect evidence only (d14, 2022 model, CoT demos): invalid but relevant and ordered reasoning kept 80-90% of the CoT benefit, while irrelevant content fell below no-CoT on GSM8K (11.0 vs 15.4). Tolerance of a wrong difference-operator table is still unmeasured.
agent_test: Inject wrong or incomplete difference-operator hints and measure success drop at equal tokens.

claim: Pure difference reduction fails on conjunctive goals when achieving one goal clobbers another (Sussman anomaly, clobbered-sibling, taxi case). Fixes are goal protection, a final all-goals check, and interleaving.
agent_test: Add a final check that all goals still hold before answer; compare error rate on multi-goal items at equal tokens.
audit_note: Norvig (PAIP ch. 4) supports clobbered-sibling, Sussman anomaly, taxi case, protected goals and achieve-all; interleaving as the fix comes from Wikipedia's Sussman anomaly entry; both are secondary or textbook sources, and the taxi case is Norvig's own toy example.

claim: Means-ends scales badly because of combinatorial blow-up, and the original authors concede the theory behind these search methods is thin.
agent_test: Boundary note only: cap decomposition depth.

claim: Graphplan-style reachability analysis beat Prodigy and UCPOP (means-ends planners) on 1990s STRIPS benchmarks, e.g. flat tire 1.1-1.3 s versus no solution found.
agent_test: LLM analogue: add a code-held reachability or relevance prune before search; test at equal tokens.

claim: Learned control rules for Prodigy helped but only partly: unsolved problems fell 218 to 135 of 500, nodes down about 17%; explanation-based learning from linear planning did not transfer to the nonlinear planner.
agent_test: Store control hints from solved items in memory; test on held-out items versus no memory at equal tokens.

claim: People solving hobbits-orcs or river crossing do not follow a pure GPS goal stack: they plan in short subsequences, and some required moves go away from the goal. A fixed noticing-order model failed on the (5,3) task. New (d01, d02, secondary full text): a fixed noticing order is not needed (120 students, all F<1); the best fit mixes means-ends with a second constraint-driven strategy chosen by probability, plus a visited-state memory and an avoid-backward-move check. Subgoal recognition came only after the subgoal was done. Thomas, Greeno, Jeffries primary texts are still paywalled and unopened (d03-d05 abstract level).
agent_test: Give the agent a second move generator (constraint-driven), a visited-state memory and an undo check next to difference reduction; allow a non-greedy move only when a loop is detected or the greedy move breaks a constraint. Compare to pure difference reduction at equal tokens. Open the 1974 and 1977 papers before treating the detour rule as human-derived.

claim: Tower of Hanoi difficulty tracks the length to the first subgoal and the problem representation (isomorph viewpoint), not only the total solution length.
agent_test: Rephrase items into two viewpoints (change-of-state vs transformation) and measure accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Mode of presentation changes Hanoi strategy: an external display raises completion; mental solving raises reported subgoal and sequence-memory use. Self-reports are the only strategy measure.
agent_test: Offer an explicit external state ledger vs none; measure completion. a29 and b22 are the same group and data, so one independent source.

claim: People do not invest early moves in exploratory learning on Hanoi; they explore and undo only when it pays at once.
agent_test: Compare a forced early probe step vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Instruction emphasis (accuracy vs effort) shifts which Hanoi strategy people use; ACT-R fits a perceptual strategy for accuracy and limited look-ahead for effort. No single strategy describes everyone.
agent_test: Route by cost: cheap perceptual heuristic vs deeper look-ahead by item size; test the router.

claim: An explicit means-ends prompt (recursive goal decomposition plus per-step state tracking) beats CoT on a continuous-state planning testbed for 6 of 7 models, tie on GPT-5.4: Claude Sonnet 4.6 77.8 to 94.5, Gemini 3 Flash 65.6 to 82.0, GPT-4o 25.7 to 36.9. Cost is 1.8 to 3.8 times CoT tokens; pass@1 beats CoT pass@3 on 4 of 7 models. Confirmed from the paper tables. Re-read (d22): thinking mode was off by design and external solvers or verifiers were excluded on purpose. Gap 1 stays open: no study tests a means-ends scaffold with thinking on. Indirect hints: a plain CoT prompt adds little for reasoning models (d13, GPQA, Gemini Flash 2.5 lost 13.1 points at the 100% metric) and thinking and non-thinking pass@k are comparable on math at equal tokens, but not on puzzles of medium difficulty (d07).
agent_test: Run MEDAKA-style arms with thinking on and off, against CoT pass@k with a code verifier, at equal tokens, on a second domain.

claim: In MEDAKA each part matters, and each alone recovers most of the gain over CoT. Claude Sonnet 4.6 (CoT 77.8, full 94.5): decomposition without state tracking 90.5 (76% of the gain), tracking plus numeric instructions without decomposition 91.0 (79%). Gemini 3 Flash (CoT 65.6, full 82.0): 76.0 (63%) and 75.1 (58%). The state-tracking arm also carries the numeric calculation instructions, so a pure ledger arm and a pure stack arm do not exist, and nothing isolates difference naming. On Gemini nonlinear problems removing the recursive module costs the most (50.9 to 28.9). Separate evidence (d17, fine-tuned Qwen2-7B): a goal-distance count (Goal CoT) hurt out of distribution while stating exact state and effects (State CoT) helped inside the trained length range.
agent_test: Four arms at equal tokens: ledger only (code-held), calculation hints only, stack only, difference naming only; then full. Report each as a share of the gain over CoT, on at least two domains.

claim: MEDAKA gains vanish for small models on hard structure (Gemma4 2B/4B, Llama nonlinear no gain), and the search-style AoT+ is worse than CoT for GPT-4o (19.8 vs 25.7) and Llama 3.3 70B (17.6 vs 26.6).
schema_part: G (scaffold must not hurt a weak model)
agent_test: Run the scaffold on a small model; keep a fallback to plain CoT if no gain.

claim: Backward chaining (goal to subgoals, with caching) beats CoT and forward Selection-Inference on deep proofs: Depth-5 relative gains +44%/+56% (ProofWriter), +37%/+113% (PrOntoQA), +43% ParaRules over CoT; calls 3.8x fewer at depth 1, 11.8x fewer at depth 5. Backward CoT alone does not clearly beat forward CoT. Confirmed from the paper text.
agent_test: Test the modular design vs single-prompt backward CoT at equal tokens; the gain belongs to the code-held modular loop.

claim: Label accuracy overstates reasoning: CoT reached correct proof chains only 28% of the time at depth 5 on ProofWriter; hallucination caused 48% of errors.
schema_part: G (verify the chain not the label)
agent_test: Score step validity, not only final answer.

claim: GPT-4o plans worse backward than forward in the model (example 53.5% vs 36% in one array setting; Blocksworld 20.5 vs 39.5 from c03), so naive backward chaining inside the model is not free; flipping the problem and combining forward and flipped samples with self-verification lifted success 4 to 24 points over 200 trials per setting. Paper text re-opened (d18). The model picks the easier direction 78.5% (undirected graphs) and 60.5% (directed graphs) of the time, and GPT-3.5 accepted every Blocksworld plan it checked.
agent_test: Compare forward, backward and flipped prompts at equal tokens per item class.

claim: Recursive decomposition only when the executor fails (ADaPT) beat ReAct, plan-then-execute and Reflexion with GPT-3.5: ALFWorld 71.6 vs 43.3/43.3/57.5, WebShop 44.0 vs 32.0/17.0/35.0, TextCraft 52.0 vs 19.0/27.0/32.0. Confirmed from the paper tables. Re-opened (d12): ADaPT was also run with GPT-4, LLaMA-2 70B and Lemur, so the result is not GPT-3.5 only, but all models are from 2023. Gain rises with the depth cap (dmax 1 to 2 to 3, largest step 1 to 2); on TextCraft the depth used grows with recipe depth (1.9 at depth 2, 2.8 at depth 3). On WebShop always-decompose (static decomposition, 17.0) was worse than the plain executor (29.0), and as-needed (44.0) beat both. No test with current or thinking models.
agent_test: Trigger decomposition only after a failed step with a depth cap of 3; compare to always-decompose and to no decomposition at equal tokens, using a current thinking model.

claim: Subgoal milestones with a checker raise long-horizon web success (Gemini-2.5-pro 23.0 to 32.1 on WebArena-Lite), but the checker is imperfect (F1 0.68).
agent_test: Add a milestone check; measure false progress accepted.

claim: Worked-example procedure prompts for Blocksworld help only when closely matched to the problem class and do not generalise to longer stacks; self-consistency lowered accuracy on these prompts.
agent_test: Vary problem size beyond example size; test whether a code-held procedure holds where a prompted one fails. b14 and c07 are the same paper. Not re-opened (PDF failed).

claim: The Shojaee et al. Hanoi collapse is partly an output-length and format artifact (10 tokens per move allows N about 12-13 at 64k; asking for code gave high accuracy at 15 disks), and the River Crossing set had impossible instances; but replications still see trouble near 8 disks. New: the Apple authors' reply (d07) puts the first Hanoi error at about move 40 of 255 (N=8), so length alone does not explain it; stepwise p-move prompting (d09) and a tool-call environment holding state (d08) still fail from about N=8 for reasoning models, up to N=8 or 10 tested.
schema_part: G (do not make the model emit long move lists)
agent_test: Have code hold and emit the long move sequence; the model chooses only the next step.

claim: Giving the model the exact Hanoi algorithm in the prompt did not move the collapse point, and a move-by-move interface with feedback made collapse start earlier. New (d08): with the environment holding the state and the model choosing each move, collapse began at lower disk counts and showed loops (about 40% deterministic reuse at n=8). Counter (d10): when the algorithm and current state are in each one-step prompt and k=3 voting with an output-length red flag is used, a 20-disk run finished with zero errors.
agent_test: Test next-move-only with code-held state at 8 to 15 disks in two arms: no algorithm given vs algorithm given, each with and without k=3 voting and a visited-state guard, at equal tokens.

claim: Splitting into single-step calls with first-to-ahead-by-3 voting solved a 20-disk Hanoi (1,048,575 steps) with zero errors in an actual completed run (corrected from 'projected'; d10). Each prompt gave the algorithm and the current state; gpt-4.1-mini, outputs over 750 tokens discarded. Single-step error rate was about 0.0045 for gpt-4.1-mini, flat as disks grew. Cost is mostly voting, and the paper itself says it covers execution, not finding the plan.
agent_test: Only test the discard-over-long-reply rule; the rest does not carry to open problems.

claim: GPT-4-class models solved about a third of Blocksworld plan generation and 2-5% on obfuscated names; o1-preview reached 97.8% plain, 52.8% Mystery, and 23.63% on 20-40 step plans. Confirmed from the o1 paper.
agent_test: Test the scaffold on obfuscated variants so gains cannot come from memorised surface patterns.
audit_note: All three sources (PlanBench 2023, o1 PlanBench 2024, LLM-Modulo position paper) come from the same Kambhampati/Valmeekam lab and reuse its benchmark; the quoted numbers (206/600, 4.3%, 2%, 97.8%, 52.8%, 23.63%) do check out.

claim: An external sound verifier with back-prompting lifts LLM plans a lot where the LLM proposes plausible plans (Blocksworld 82% in 15 rounds, Logistics 70%, Mystery about 10%).
agent_test: Add a code validator loop; the gain is bounded by proposal quality. c10 reports numbers from other papers.

claim: Restating the current state in the prompt (memoization) cuts state hallucination, and random search trajectories in the examples work as well as human-chosen ones (Game of 24 70.0 vs 71.0).
agent_test: Add a per-step state restatement; ablate.
audit_note: Only Sel et al. (AoT+) supports the claim (its other listed entries are the same paper); the second distinct source (MEDAKA) actually reports state hallucination and drift persisting in AoT+ traces. The 70.0 vs 71.0 Game of 24 numbers and memoization argument do check out in AoT+.

claim: Plan abstraction (solve a simplified problem first, then use it as a plan) can give illusory plans; no false-plan rate has been measured.
agent_test: Measure how often an abstract plan fails at the detailed level on our items.

claim: LLMs are poor verifiers of hard constraints (travel planning verifier pass rate 0.455-0.489, barely above chance) and poor solvers alone; LLM-written natural-language action prompts match hand-written ones.
schema_part: G (do not trust an LLM-only verifier)
agent_test: Measure the model's own verifier accuracy on our items before relying on it.

claim: Putting the transition and goal test in code removes the search burden on puzzles with a clear goal: GPT-4 wrote the successor function and goal test once, and plain BFS or DFS solved all 1,362 24-game items, all 502 BlocksWorld items (4-5 blocks), all 4,000 PrOntoQA items and the 20 mini crosswords with a few model calls.
agent_test: For items with an explicit goal test, let the model write the check once and run search in code. Measure items with no clear goal state separately, where this route is closed.

claim: Candidate rule for non-greedy moves (hypothesis built from d02, d06, d08, d19): allow a move that does not reduce the named difference only when (a) a loop is detected (state already visited), (b) the greedy move would break a stated constraint, or (c) no operator reduces the difference. A reset to the start state is a sanctioned non-greedy move. Not yet tested on an LLM.
agent_test: Pure difference reduction vs the three-trigger rule vs unrestricted moves, on hobbits-orcs style and Blocksworld items, equal tokens; count loops and solved items.

claim: A model checking its own progress without a sound outside signal is unreliable: GPT-4 as verifier had false-negative rates of 20.7% (Game of 24), 95.8% (graph colouring) and 97.1% (Mystery Blocksworld); intrinsic self-correction lowered GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA from 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-3.5 accepted every Blocksworld plan. A fine-tuned 7B detector reached precision 90.5% and recall 99.2% for wrong steps but validity did not improve. The accuracy a checker needs before subgoal checks help is not measured.
agent_test: Subgoal check by recomputing state from the code-held ledger; compare against model-judged checks and against plain resampling, equal tokens; log false progress accepted.

claim: Experience memory for LLM agents helps for near transfer and weakens with distance: ExpeL insights moved from HotpotQA to FEVER (ReAct 63, transfer 65 without and 70 with target examples); AWM online memory beat baseline by 8.9 to 14.0 points across websites and domains, while offline memory lost its edge as the train-test gap widened. No test of control-rule memory across problem classes for planning.
agent_test: Store hints with a problem-class tag, retire them on a class change, and compare same-class vs cross-class reuse at equal tokens.

claim: Gap 3 is mostly open. Positive transfer of explicit decomposition or goal-directed prompting exists on ALFWorld, WebShop, TextCraft (ADaPT), deduction (LAMBADA) and mixing (MEDAKA). Negative or null: Goal CoT hurt out-of-distribution (d17) and search-style prompts hurt some models (K14). No study found for ARC grids, code, or open questions without a goal state.
agent_test: Run the same means-ends arm on ARC items, code-repair items and an open question set with no clear goal state; keep it off where it does not beat CoT at equal tokens.

claim: No study measuring how often goal clobbering (Sussman type) shows up in LLM outputs on multi-goal items was found. Closest hints: MEDAKA multi-goal items gain strongly from decomposition (Claude 50.4 to 89.5), stepwise goal-directed agents loop in cul-de-sacs (d19), and a final all-goals check was not tested anywhere.
agent_test: Tag multi-goal items, log whether any earlier-satisfied goal is false in the final state, and compare with and without a code-run final all-goals check.
